requirement_vague: Verify multiple comments can be added to the same article with unique IDs
requirement_precise: Create user1 (username: 'multicommentuser1', email: 'multicommentuser1@test.com', password: 'pass123'). User1 creates an article 'Multi Comment Article'. User1 adds comment 'First comment'. User1 adds comment 'Second comment'. User1 adds comment 'Third comment'. GET /api/articles/{slug}/comments. Verify 3 comments are returned. Verify each comment has a unique id (no duplicates). Verify the comment bodies are preserved correctly. This tests comment creation and persistence with multiple comments.

implementation.code_reference:
class Comment(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: Optional[int] = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
...
comment = Comment(body=body, created_at=ts, updated_at=ts, author_id=current_user.id, article_id=article.id)
session.add(comment)
session.commit()
...
comments = sorted(article.comments, key=lambda c: c.id or 0)
return {"comments": [comment_dict(c, viewer, session) for c in comments]}
implementation.reasoning: The service persists each new comment as a separate Comment row linked by article_id, so multiple comments can be added to the same article. Because Comment.id is an auto-generated primary key and GET /api/articles/{slug}/comments returns all article.comments with each comment's id and body, three added comments will be returned with distinct IDs and preserved bodies.
